chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Read what the un-packaged run did
Make Claude show its work, make it dig
Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader loses the thread when a pronoun/noun has no antecedent they can hold. Re-walked all 12 chunks against the current working-tree body (uncommitted diff drops the single word 'A' from chunk 4's 'A separate Claude session reads...' -> 'Separate Claude session reads...'; unrelated to referents). Chunk 4's Phase-3 menu: 'LLM judge.' (line 65) is introduced fresh with its own explanatory sentence ('Separate Claude session reads the produced work and judges it: an opinion, not a pass-fail script'), no forward reference. Line 69's instruction 'Drop the shape name after the colon, one of: judge, shell-hook, Ralph re-feed' resolves each abbreviated token against the three bolded handles two lines above in the SAME chunk: judge<-LLM judge, shell-hook<-Deterministic shell-hook, Ralph re-feed<-Ralph re-feed (verbatim) -- confirmed by reading curriculum/prompts/diagnose-and-resend-4.md, which branches on the identical three tokens ('If shell-hook:'/'If judge:'/'If Ralph re-feed:'), so the instruction line's shorthand is the same vocabulary the prompt itself uses, not a drifted label. Chunk 0 line 15 'three failure-mode lenses' sets up chunk 1; chunk 6's Reference/plan.md handles echo chunk 0 line 17. No unresolved referent found. Harm absent.

Harm: a callback that depends on which file/module sits where breaks under re-sequencing. Chunk 2 line 44 'Same prior as the repo read in Module 1' names the source by module number and unpacks the claim (the misrepresentation prior) in the same sentence. Chunk 9 line 117 names the linked doc in its own link text ('[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)') -- navigational pointer, not narrative callback. Chunk 10 (module-flag branch) line 131 names the target module by number ('Module 6'), not by position. No positional phrasing ('above'/'the opening lecture') found in body. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the module's current file set doesn't have strands the reader. Chunk 10 line 131 'The walk-away report at the close is what Module 6 opens on' -- host module learn-from-the-test sits immediately before spot-gaps-build-the-loop (M6) in the MODULES array (site/layouts/curriculum.js), unchanged from prior audit. Line 133 'Same cancel-is-legit rule as the un-packaged session' resolves to the M4 beat in set-the-markers-send-it-off.md / test-and-learn.md. Neither backward reference is affected by this diff (word-trim + maintainer-only rewording). Harm absent.

Harm: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet projects as a slide that says nothing standalone. Shortest chunk is chunk 8 'Approve' (9 words, per check-slide-size.js --report this session): 'Say *lock it in.* The agent writes both files.' -- names trigger phrase and concrete effect, self-carrying. Chunk 4 (the diffed chunk) carries 4 bullets plus a fenced prompt, well past orphan threshold. Harm absent.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a reader who only skims headers. 'Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure' (line 59) is a true summary of its own chunk: three verifier-shape options plus the ask-Claude instruction to build one against the worst-cost failure. The word-trim did not touch the header or its match to content. Harm absent.

Harm: repo-authored prose tics read as filler once wall-projected. Ran `grep -niE 'not [a-z]+\.[[:space:]]*not [a-z]+\.' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md`: 0 hits. Ran `grep -niE 'one of the most|most useful|most powerful|best way|most important' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md`: 0 hits. Re-read chunk 4's post-trim bullet 'Separate Claude session reads the produced work and judges it: an opinion, not a pass-fail script.' -- one clean sentence, no anaphora triple, no verb-triplet-with-empty-leg, no abstraction-noun stack. The colon construction ('opinion, not a pass-fail script') is a contrast pair, not the banned 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple shape (only two clauses, no period-separated triple). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary smuggled onto a slide reads as unparseable jargon to an engineer in the room. Ran `grep -niE '\bsurface\b|\bcompendium\b|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|firing|Connections' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md`: all hits land past the maintainer cut (line 141+), 0 in body (lines 1-140). 'LLM judge' (chunk 4) is the ordinary LLM-as-judge evals pattern, audience-appropriate for AE101 engineer ICs, not this repo's internal class-judge system -- `grep -n '\beval\b'` this session: both hits past the maintainer cut. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-monoculture buries the actual handles and reads as noise once wall-projected. Chunk 4 carries 3 bold spans, one per verifier-shape bullet ('LLM judge' 2 words / 'Deterministic shell-hook' 2 words / 'Ralph re-feed' 3 words) -- all inside the ~5-word handle cap, and the chunk is a menu-of-options slide (student picks one shape to build), matching the reading-list/menu carve-out that lifts the per-slide budget while the handle cap still binds. The word-trim did not add or remove any bold span. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible to the layout a reader is actually in reads as silently missing. File is reached via a standalone-paragraph include link at learn-from-the-test.md:50, wrapped under .phase--exercise, reaching buildDeckModel. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report` this session reports exactly 10 non-flag slides -- applyContentFlags is being exercised by the same pipeline the diff runs through. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered or inconsistent Phase/Step ordinals strand in-file cross-references. Phase headers run 1-5 consecutively (chunks 1,3,4,7,9), unaffected by the single-word body trim. In-file forward ref 'Fire it once before Phase 4' (chunk 5) resolves to the real Phase 4 header (chunk 7). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at ##. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md`: OK, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut. The one below-shaped phrase, chunk 10 line 125 'the re-send prompt below stands alone,' points at the fenced prompt on line 129 -- same chunk. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead in-deck link, or one unnamed/geometry-located. One link in body, chunk 9 line 117, 'What packaging is' -> lectures/what-packaging-is.md, named in its own link text, not located by page position. Unaffected by the diff. Harm absent; explicitly a review surface, never a gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: MECHANICAL, run this session: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report` -> 'Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure' now reads 210 words / 4 bullets (was 211 before this diff's one-word trim of 'A separate Claude session' -> 'Separate Claude session'); footer reports 'oversized: 0' across all 10 non-flag slides. Cap met exactly, no accept-note needed. Harm (an over-cap chunk shipping unnoticed) is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an exercise heading phrased as a lecture-style claim blurs the imperative-vs-declarative mood signal the deck relies on. All 11 `##` headers are imperative or 'Phase N:' phase labels, or catalogue-style topic-noun labels naming their subject ('The reference and plan.md') -- carve-out. 'Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure' (the diffed chunk's own header) is unchanged and is an imperative phase label. No declarative-claim heading found. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a doctrine-restatement, self-referential design-commentary, or aphorism-kicker bullet reads as rigour while adding nothing. Re-read chunk 4's post-trim 'LLM judge' bullet: 'Separate Claude session reads the produced work and judges it: an opinion, not a pass-fail script. Right when the failure was qualitative...' -- this is a substantive contrast against the deterministic shell-hook bullet immediately below it (opinion vs pass-fail), not a doctrine restatement, self-referential commentary, or aphorism kicker. No other bullet in body changed by this diff. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal instruction whose answer is narrated above it spoils the beat on a text read. Read all 12 chunks: the file's shape is diagnose -> match -> build -> prove -> assemble -> resend; no guess/predict-then-reveal construction exists anywhere in body. Rule doesn't apply.

mechanical: /\b(delve|delving|honest|honestly|importantly|crucial|crucially|substrate|synergize|paradigm shift)\b/ over body projection curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--diagnose-and-resend.body.txt → 0 hits; pattern proven against planted violation.
